question: In 2025, where has India’s first zoo-based wildlife bio bank been established?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India’s first zoo-based wildlife bio bank** has been established at **Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park**, located in **Darjeeling, West Bengal**.
 
• It was set up in **2025** to preserve **genetic material** like DNA, gametes, and tissues of endangered species for conservation and research purposes.
 
• The bio bank aims to aid the conservation of rare and endangered species, especially those native to the Himalayan region, such as the **red panda**, **snow leopard**, and **clouded leopard**.
 
• The facility will also enable advanced studies on wildlife genetics, reproduction, and disease control to ensure the survival of species facing extinction.
 
• This initiative aligns with India’s **National Wildlife Action Plan** and global biodiversity conservation goals set by organizations like the **IUCN** (International Union for Conservation of Nature).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park**:

 
 
• Established in **1958**, it is known for its focus on the conservation of Himalayan fauna.
 
• It is the **largest high-altitude zoo** in India and houses several rare and endangered species.
 
• Notable species include the **red panda**, **snow leopard**, and **Siberian tiger**.
 
• The zoo is also recognized for its successful breeding programs for high-altitude animals.
 
 
 
• **Wildlife Bio Bank Concept:**
 
 
• Bio banks store **biological materials** such as DNA, tissues, and gametes for research, conservation, and reproduction purposes.
 
• They play a vital role in **ex-situ conservation**, especially for species with declining populations due to habitat destruction or climate change.
 
• Examples of global bio banks include the **Frozen Ark Project** and the **San Diego Zoo’s Frozen Zoo**.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Efforts in India:**
 
 
• India has launched several initiatives like **Project Tiger (1973)**, **Project Elephant (1992)**, and the **National Wildlife Action Plan** to protect endangered species.
 
• The **Wildlife Protection Act of 1972** provides the legal framework for protecting flora and fauna in India.
 
• Under the act, species are classified into schedules, with Schedule I offering the highest level of protection.
 
 
 
• **Red Panda Conservation:**
 
 
• The red panda is native to the Himalayan region and is classified as **Endangered** by the **IUCN**.
 
• Its population has declined due to habitat loss, poaching, and climate change.
 
• Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park has been actively involved in **breeding programs** to increase the population of red pandas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Zoological Parks in India:**

 
 
• **Mahendra Chaudhury Zoological Park:** Located in Punjab, it focuses on the conservation of native wildlife species.
 
• **Nandankanan Zoological Park:** Situated in Odisha, it is renowned for its white tiger conservation program.
 
• **Nehru Zoological Park:** Located in Hyderabad, it is one of India’s largest zoos, housing over 1,500 species of animals.
 
 
 
• **Global Efforts for Wildlife Conservation:**
 
 
• Organizations like the **IUCN**, **WWF**, and **CITES** work globally to protect endangered species.
 
• International agreements such as the **Convention on Biological Diversity** aim to promote sustainable use and conservation of biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Technological Advances in Conservation:**
 
 
• Use of **genetic analysis** and **AI-based monitoring systems** to track wildlife populations.
 
• Development of **cryopreservation techniques** for storing gametes and embryos.
